title: Flat Tag Identity
summary: shipped flat canonical tag IDs while retaining exactly one group as independent classification data
content_html:
Flat Tag Identity

Result

A canonical tag has one globally unique normalized tag_id such as moss and exactly one scalar group such as subject. The group is classification data, not part of identity: subject:moss is no longer a canonical ID, and a groups array is not supported.

Assignments and aliases continue to refer directly to tag_id. Group filters, alias constraints, styling, coverage, and scoring resolve the tag's group from the registry instead of parsing the ID. Interpretative meaning belongs in the tag's document after Tag-document linking; that document does not create additional identities or group memberships.

Why this is separate

Flattening identity changes canonical registry keys and every assignment and alias that refers to them. It also requires verification that earlier namespaced collisions have been resolved to one globally unique name and one group. That is a coherent vocabulary migration, not part of document association or group-based reporting.

The existing registry description remains available through this feature so Tag-document linking can use it as one-time seed content. Removing that field before the documents exist would discard the current semantic source.

Feature Documents

  • Flat Tag Identity Concept — the lasting identity and ownership model.
  • Flat Tag Identity Delivery — the completed schema, data, service, and UI migration with cutover evidence.
  • Tag Registry Label Retirement Delivery — the proposed follow-on removal of the registry label now duplicated by the flat tag ID.

Boundary

  • Tag Vocabulary Import Retirement removes obsolete bulk paths before this feature changes canonical identity.
  • This feature owns flat IDs, collision-decision verification, reference migration, the one-group invariant, and removal of group-prefix parsing.
  • It retains the group taxonomy, allowed-group policy, group-driven UI and analysis, and the current series/work assignment model.
  • It does not create or associate documents, remove registry descriptions, or implement semantic-token targets.
  • Tag-document linking follows this feature and establishes the required registry-to-document relationship.

Durable Destinations

Shipped identity and source ownership belong in Tag Source Data, Tag Registry, and Tag Aliases. Assignment consequences belong in Series Tags and Series Tag Editor.
